inputs.text:
You will control a camera that starts at the viewpoint of this photo, at standing eye height. Convert the movement instruction into primitive steps, in order. Use ONLY what the instruction says.
Instruction: "I walk near the counter, then turn right, walk into the hallway and turn around to face where I come from."
Primitives (JSON objects):
- {"op":"forward","amount":"default|few_steps"}  walk straight ahead without a named target
- {"op":"back","direction":"left|right|null"}  step backwards (optionally back-left/right)
- {"op":"turn","direction":"left|right","amount":"slight|normal|around"}  turn in place; "turn around" is amount around
- {"op":"go","target":"...","relation":"to|near|next_to|beside|into|through|past","side":"left|right|null"}  walk to/near/past/through a target
- {"op":"face","target":"..."}  turn in place to face an object (also "look at"/"look through")
- {"op":"face_start"}  turn in place to face the starting point
- {"op":"face_motion"}  keep facing the walking direction
Target descriptions must uniquely identify the object as seen in the photo when possible: include color, material, relative position in the photo (left/right/center, near/far) exactly as implied by the instruction. If the target is not visible in the photo, still describe it from the instruction. Return {"steps":[...]}

steps.target: the bar counter on the right with black chairs

inputs.text: Above: the original starting photo. Below: six views from the camera's CURRENT position in a blurry 3D reconstruction of the same place. View k is rotated 60*k degrees to the right of the current facing direction.
